title: Function calling parse debug scratchpad (maya 7)
content:
Context: Quick personal notes while investigating recurring parsing failures for function/tool-calling structured outputs. Repro is intermittent (5-15% of calls) and seems correlated with streaming + multi-part responses and specific models (open models with temperature > 0.3).

Problem summary:
- Symptoms: downstream JSON parsing fails when we try to parse model text->JSON for function calls. Client error seen: JSONDecodeError or parser returning null because output contains trailing text.
- Observed errors: 
  - 'JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' (empty string fed to json.loads)
  - 'ExtraData: Extra data: line 1 column 234 (char 233)' (model emitted two JSON objects concatenated)
  - partial JSON (truncated) because stream cut mid-object
  - function signature mismatch: model returned key 'user_id' as number in some runs and as string in others -> validation fails in typed schema

What I tried so far (commands / quick hacks):
1) Reproduce with CLI curl + streaming chunk test:
   - POST /v1/completions with streaming: true, model=openlm-7b-qlora (local) using my test prompt.
   - Observed stream chunk with: '{"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "{\"task_id\": 123, \"result\": \"ok\"}\nExtra:"}}]}'
   - Parsing code was using simple join of chunks then json.loads -> fails because of trailing 'Extra:' text.

2) Robust parsers: tried python 'json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode' to extract the first JSON object then ignore rest -> mitigates ExtraData but not empty strings or truncated objects.

3) Add regex wrapper to find first '{'.. matching '}' pair by naive bracket counting. Works for many cases but fails if model includes nested braces in strings or escaped braces.

4) Response format enforcement: tried adding clear system message: 'You must only output a single valid JSON object and nothing else.' Reduced but did not eliminate.

5) Use assistant function calling (model.function_call) with explicit function schema (name, params JSON schema). Observed two failure modes:
   - Model calls function but param object is slightly off (missing required field) -> server returns function_call with arguments string that is invalid JSON (unquoted keys or trailing commas).
   - Model outputs plain text instead of function_call in ~8% runs (maybe due to temperature).

Error snippets captured (copied from logs):
- '{"task_id": 101, "status": "done"}\nNote: processed 1/1'  -> Extra trailing note after JSON
- '{"id": 42,"result": "ok", }' -> trailing comma
- '{"id": 42,"result": "ok"}{"id":43"..' -> concatenated objects
- streaming chunk break: '{\"id\": 9, \"outp\"\n'

Hypotheses:
- Streaming and partial flushes cause mid-object truncation; client assembly logic sometimes treats newline boundary as object boundary.
- Some models (or tokenizers) prefer to inject commentary unless heavily constrained by system prompts; mixed-mode responses (function_call+comment) observed.
- When temperature > 0.0, model occasionally adds small textual notes after producing required JSON (e.g., 'Done', 'OK', 'Processed') which breaks strict parsers.
- Function schema enforcement in API might not be strict enough for some open models; they attempt to mimic function signature but produce non-JSON args.
- Race condition: background middleware that strips control tokens can drop the trailing '}' if it sits alone in a chunk. Need to validate chunk assembly.

Immediate mitigations (what to run next):
- Harden client parsing pipeline: 3-tier approach
  1) Try json.loads on joined text.
  2) If fails, attempt raw_decode to get first object; if successful, log leftover and continue.
  3) If raw_decode fails, attempt bracket-balance scan but only accept if bracket count back to zero and no unescaped quotes bridging chunks.
- Add streaming chunk integrity check: track open quotes and braces across chunks. If chunk boundary splits a quoted string, mark for reassembly and avoid naive parse.
- Ingest telemetry: add counters for failure mode types (empty, extradata, truncated, invalid-json) and record model, temp, prompt-id.
- Force response_mode=structured (if API supports) or set temperature=0.0 for critical calls.

Longer-term fixes / engineering items:
- Update function-calling guide for open models: require stricter system priming + example with 'ONLY OUTPUT JSON' + negative examples. (Link: Confluence draft)
- Add server-side post-processing step that attempts to sanitize model output before returning to client (strip trailing notes if they follow a valid JSON object). Need to design for safety (avoid dropping legitimately important text).
- Explore using a micro-parser (LLM-based repair): if parsing fails, call a constrained model to transform free text to valid JSON given schema. This is more costy but might be useful as fallback.

Notes / small experiments to run next:
- Re-run failing workload with temperature=0.0 and stream=true to isolate streaming vs randomness.
- Capture raw token-level stream for 200 failed calls and manual inspect chunk boundaries.
- Test JSONDecoder.raw_decode across a corpus of 500 outputs to measure how many are salvageable.

TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Add failure-mode telemetry metric (INF-telemetry)
- [ ] Create small test harness that feeds concatenated chunks with simulated truncated boundaries
- [ ] File small patch to assembly logic to preserve trailing control characters and check bracket/quote parity before parsing
- [ ] Sync with Ashwin re: kernel that strips control tokens (possible root cause)

Breadcrumbs / references:
- JIRA-INF-2142 (linked) is the customer incident mentioning same symptoms
- PR 892 (runtime) changed streaming buffer behavior last month -> revert to confirm

If I don't get to this later: quick note to self: most immediate wins are defensive parsing + telemetry. If that reduces customer-visible failures, we can then invest in model-side priming and server-side repairs.

End of scratchpad.
